Title: No repeat of Dataran Merdeka mess, says Hannah Yeoh
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Members of the public attending the 2026 National Day celebration at Dataran Putrajaya on Aug 31 have been urged to act responsibly by disposing of their rubbish at designated areas to ensure the venue remains clean.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said she did not want a repeat of the recent incident at Dataran Merdeka, Kuala Lumpur, where large amounts of rubbish were left behind following a public gathering.
"Maintaining cleanliness is a shared responsibility. It is not solely the responsibility of Putrajaya Corporation (PPj) to collect rubbish after an event.
"Imagine coming to celebrate National Day, only to leave behind an area covered with rubbish. I do not think that creates a good impression, and I urge everyone present to dispose of their waste in the bins provided," she told reporters after officiating the Madani Kita (PMK) programme with the Putrajaya Federal Territory community today.
The event was also attended by PPj president Datuk Mohd Sakeri Abdul Kadir.
During the programme, Hannah presented mock cheques representing a special contribution of RM5,000 from Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to selected Kawasan Rukun Tetangga or Neighbourhood Watch areas.
Hannah said her office was currently focusing on efforts to raise public awareness and believes the public has learned from the recent rubbish accumulation incident at Dataran Merdeka.
She added that PPj would increase the number of rubbish bins at strategic locations and enhance waste collection frequency to ensure the celebration area remains clean and comfortable.
"I will also ensure that PPj issues reminders and announcements to everyone present to dispose of their rubbish properly. This is a shared responsibility and not just the duty of local authorities to clean up after an event," she said.
On July 20, Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) conducted cleanup operations at
Dataran Merdeka
after the area was left littered following a large gathering to watch the live broadcast of the 2026 FIFA World Cup final.
DBKL said waste collection would continue, but added that maintaining the cleanliness of the capital should not depend solely on the efforts of cleaning workers after the public has left.
The 2026 National Day celebration would be held at Dataran Putrajaya on Aug 31 on a moderate yet vibrant scale.
"Malaysia Madani: Kesejahteraan Dinikmati" has been selected as the theme for the 2026 National Day and Malaysia Day (HKHM2026) celebrations, while the Malaysia Madani logo will continue to be used as the official logo for the celebrations until next year.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Homecoming rush: Voters return, traffic builds across Negri Sembilan
Article:
SEREMBAN: Traffic flow on several major routes around Seremban, as well as connecting roads to outlying districts such as Bukit Putus, Kuala Pilah and Kuala Klawang in Jelebu, has been reported to be steadily building since early this morning.
The surge is attributed to outstation voters returning to their hometowns to cast their ballots in the 16th Negri Sembilan election.
Real-time traffic checks on Google Maps, Waze and Apple Maps revealed slow-moving traffic at several hotspots, particularly along the Seremban-Kuala Pilah road through Bukit Putus, the Seremban-Tampin route, and roads leading to Kuala Klawang in Jelebu.
Rain in several areas of the district around midday further compounded the situation.
In Seremban city centre, a Bernama survey observed a marked increase in vehicles on several main roads, with motorists believed to be making their way to polling centres, most of which are situated close to major thoroughfares.
Over in villages, the typically quiet weekend atmosphere has also transformed, with rows of vehicles lining narrow roads, while eateries and breakfast stalls have been enjoying increased patronage from larger crowds than usual.
Meanwhile, Negri Sembilan Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department chief Supt Roslan Mohamed@Ab Aziz, when contacted, said conditions remained under control as of 2pm despite the noticeable increase in vehicles.
"There have been some delays at toll plazas due to the higher volume of vehicles entering Negri Sembilan, but traffic personnel have been deployed at key locations to help ease the flow and manage the situation," he said.
He added that police expected the number of vehicles to continue rising towards the evening peak period, but monitoring and on-ground deployment of personnel would be maintained to ensure traffic flow remains manageable.
Today, 859,760 voters across Negri Sembilan are fulfilling their duty to elect new representatives for 36 state assembly seats, ultimately determining the state government for the next term.

Title: Tun Jugah-inspired hairstyle draws crowds at KJH Sarawak
Article:
KUCHING: Sarawak Tourism Board (STB) marketing administrative officer Ozie Tunggeng has been turning heads at the Karnival Jom Heboh (KJH) Sarawak Segulai Sejalai with a distinctive hairstyle inspired by the legendary Iban leader, Tun Jugah anak Barieng.
Ozie said his unique appearance has attracted the curiosity of visitors, particularly those from Peninsular Malaysia, who are keen to learn more about his background and heritage.
"Many visitors come up to ask where I am from and what my ethnicity is because they are intrigued by my appearance," he said when met at the STB booth during the carnival.
"I am a Bidayuh from Bau, but my grandmother is Iban, and I can speak several Sarawakian dialects."
Ozie said he adopted the iconic look to reflect his role as a cultural activist while promoting Sarawak as a tourism destination.
Throughout the carnival, Ozie has been promoting the state's tourism products and hosting interactive stage activities, including tourism quizzes.
Now participating in KJH for the third time, he said the carnival continues to attract overwhelming public interest, making it an ideal platform to engage directly with visitors.
STB assistant marketing officer Nabil Aiman Sait said the board remains committed to promoting Sarawak's tourism offerings to both domestic and international visitors.
He said one of its key priorities is raising awareness of lesser-known attractions, including the state's national parks and nature reserves.
"Many locals are still unaware of the full range of Sarawak's tourism offerings, including admission fees for certain destinations.
"KJH provides us with an excellent platform to share accurate and up-to-date information with visitors," he said.
Nabil said STB's third consecutive participation in the carnival had delivered encouraging results by increasing public awareness of the state's tourism assets.
He also encouraged Sarawakians to explore their home state before travelling abroad.
Echoing similar sentiments, SarawakTourism, Creative Industry and Performing Arts Ministry assistant administrative officer Norasma Faiznur Bujang said they had brought together all agencies under its purview to showcase a wide range of initiatives throughout the carnival.
Besides promoting tourism and the creative industry, she said the ministry is also raising public awareness of the upcoming 2027 SEA Games in Sarawak as part of efforts to strengthen the state's position as a leading regional destination for major international events.

Title: Mental health stigma leaves many suffering in silence, says Queen
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia, has expressed concern that the stigma surrounding mental health continues to prevent many people from seeking professional help, leaving them to suffer in silence.
Citing New Straits Times reports on the growing mental health crisis, Her Majesty said adults were increasingly burdened by financial hardship, debt and strained family relationships, often leading to severe psychological distress.
"Studies carried out by NST also show that 16.5 per cent of children aged five to 15 struggle with mental health problems.
"And one in four adolescents aged 13 to 17 experiences depression," Her Majesty said at the University of Reading Malaysia's 10th convocation ceremony today.
Raja Zarith Sofiah, who received an Honorary Doctorate in Psychology from the university, said addressing the nation's mental health challenges had never been more important.
She said understanding human behaviour, resilience and relationships was fundamental to building stronger communities and a more harmonious society.
Her Majesty also lamented the rise of hate speech and growing intolerance despite unprecedented access to information.
"It is a sad irony that, at a time when knowledge is more accessible than ever through websites, social media and podcasts, we have become less tolerant, less kind, and continue to focus on our differences rather than our shared humanity," she said.
Raja Zarith Sofiah said universities must do more than equip graduates with technical knowledge, stressing the need to nurture character, sound judgement and strong moral values.
Quoting the late Royal Professor Tan Sri Dr Syed Muhammad Naquib Al-Attas, she said the true purpose of education was to cultivate virtuous individuals, not merely skilled workers.
Citing the teachings of Imam al-Ghazali that knowledge without action is of little value, the Queen urged graduates to use what they had learned for the greater good.
Her Majesty also thanked the university for the honorary doctorate and congratulated the graduates, reminding them that their success would ultimately be measured by the positive impact they make on society.

Title: Nerves, pride as 1st time voters cast their ballots
Article:
SEREMBAN: For many first-time voters in the 16th Negri Sembilan election today, casting their ballot was a memorable milestone marked by excitement, nerves and pride.
Fashion designer Hani Eriqa Mazlan, 21, said voting for the first time gave her a deeper appreciation of the democratic process.
"I was nervous and my hands were shaking because it was my first time voting. I had always known about elections, but going through the process myself felt completely different.
"I have followed the issues and know what is best for Negri Sembilan. Today, we make our choice," she said after voting at Sekolah Menengah Agama Dato' Klana Petra Maamor.
Hani Eriqa arrived with her younger sister, Hani Mazri Eyna, 20, who was also voting for the first time, along with five other family members.
The college student said the experience reinforced the importance of every vote in choosing representatives who would champion the people's interests.
"I was a little nervous but also excited because it was my first opportunity to fulfil my responsibility as a voter," she said.
Meanwhile, college student M. Lavinesh Nair, 18, said he initially felt overwhelmed by the large crowd when he arrived at the polling centre with his family.
"I was nervous because there were so many people and I was a little confused at first. But the Election Commission officers were very helpful and guided me through the process.
"Now that I have voted, I know what the experience is really like," he said.
As of 11am, voter turnout stood at 28.11 per cent.
A total of 859,760 registered voters, including 7,391 postal voters, are eligible to vote today to elect representatives for the state's 36 legislative assembly seats, with 103 candidates contesting.
Early voting on July 28 recorded a turnout of 91.06 per cent, with 14,995 voters casting their ballots, surpassing the Election Commission's 90 per cent target.

Title: CAP calls for tougher screening for pilots after Jakarta drug case
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The Consumers' Association of Penang (CAP) has called for tougher screening and continuous monitoring of pilots following the arrest of a Malaysian pilot in Jakarta over alleged drug smuggling.
CAP president Mohideen Abdul Kader said the association was "shocked and disappointed" by the incident, calling it a major blow to Malaysia's aviation industry and public confidence in air travel.
He said passenger safety must remain the highest priority, as travellers entrust their lives to pilots every time they board an aircraft.
"Passengers expect pilots to be responsible for their lives on a flight. They have the right to expect pilots to be physically and mentally fit because they pay for their flight tickets.
"We urge airlines to strengthen their recruitment processes by ensuring pilots are free from tobacco, alcohol and drugs, while introducing stricter health monitoring throughout their careers," he said today.
It was reported yesterday that a Malaysian pilot was arrested for allegedly attempting to smuggle a large quantity of drugs, including more than 70,000 ecstasy pills weighing 25kg, into Indonesia recently.
In reports published by Kompas.com and Suara.com, Indonesian authorities also found 2.74g of methamphetamine, as well as 0.0825g of methamphetamine residue in a glass pipe, when the suspect was arrested at Terminal 3 of Soekarno-Hatta Airport about 11.30pm local time on Tuesday.
Mohideen said all pilots and co-pilots should undergo thorough medical examinations and fitness assessments before operating flights to ensure they are
fit to fly
.
"The bigger issue is whether the alleged drug use could have been detected earlier through mandatory medical examinations and fitness assessments. This is an area that requires stricter monitoring," he added.
Mohideen also called on cabin crew members to report to the relevant authorities any suspicious behaviour or signs that a pilot might be unfit for duty.
"We are talking about the lives of hundreds of passengers, including children. Even if such incidents are rare, precautions are essential because there is no room for complacency when it comes to aviation safety," he said.
He stressed that the actions of a small number of undisciplined pilots should not tarnish the reputation of the many professionals in the industry.
Mohideen described the incident as a "major embarrassment" for Malaysia's aviation sector and said stronger preventive measures were needed to maintain public confidence and ensure the highest standards of flight safety.

Title: Bukit Aman to work with Indonesian police in probe involving Malaysian pilot
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bukit Aman will work closely with their Indonesian counterparts in the investigation involving a Malaysian pilot arrested in Indonesia for allegedly attempting to smuggle drugs into the country.
Bukit Aman Narcotic Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan told the New Straits Times that police are awaiting more information from Indonesian authorities before determining the next course of action.
"Once we receive it, we will assess the information and determine the appropriate follow-up action," he said.
Hussein said police are also studying the need to send a team of investigators to Indonesia to interview the suspect to establish the full circumstances surrounding the case.
He said among the key aspects under investigation is identifying where the suspect obtained the drugs and whether he was acting on behalf of, or in collaboration with, a drug trafficking syndicate.
"We also want to determine how many times the suspect may have carried out similar operations, and whether he is part of a larger network.
Investigators are also looking into how the suspect allegedly managed to smuggle the drugs through airport security in Malaysia before departing for Indonesia.
The findings, Hussein said, would be crucial in identifying any weaknesses that may have been exploited.
It was reported that the 39-year-old suspect had operated Malaysia Airlines flight MH727 from Kuala Lumpur to Jakarta before he was arrested at Terminal 3 of Soekarno-Hatta Airport on Tuesday night with 70,000 ecstasy pills.
He was also tested positive for three types of drugs — meth, MDMA and cocaine — after he landed in Jakarta.
Indonesian Police Narcotics Crime Directorate director Brigadier General Eko Hadi Santoso said Customs officers decided to inspect the suspect's suitcase after detecting something suspicious during an X-ray scan at the international arrivals area.
"Checks showed that officers found 14 large packages containing ecstasy and one packet containing methamphetamine," he was quoted as saying.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police tighten security, urge supporters to accept poll results
Article:
SEREMBAN: Police have urged political party supporters to remain calm and accept the outcome of the Negri Sembilan election, with security measures in place to handle any eventuality.
Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said police were prepared to manage any situation, including a possible change in the state administration following the election results.
He advised supporters of winning parties to remain disciplined and comply with instructions from the authorities.
"Police are responsible for maintaining security not only before and during the election, but also after polling.
"In the post-election period, there may be attempts by certain quarters to provoke others if there is a change in leadership or dissatisfaction among supporters of either the winners or losers. That is our concern," he told reporters after visiting the polling centre at SMK King George V today.
Khalid said security monitoring had been increased at key installations and strategic locations, including the state secretariat, palace, government offices and other related premises.
He urged supporters to cooperate with police and assured that officers were ready to respond swiftly to any incidents.
He said police had identified 26 election hotspots statewide based on previous records of clashes and deployed Cantas rapid response teams to each location.
"These hotspots were identified based on our experience and records of past incidents.
"Although we have not received any reports of such incidents so far, we are maintaining a stronger police presence.
"Each state constituency has two Cantas teams to ensure security and public order remain under control in these areas," he said.
Each team comprises eight officers and personnel equipped with technical equipment and body-worn cameras to monitor activities at polling centres and other key locations.

Title: Local councils must review dog-catching procedures
Article:
LETTER
: I am deeply saddened and disturbed by the death of Rocky, the dog that died during a round-up of strays in Klang.
The circumstances surrounding his death have caused widespread public outrage.
The killing of Rocky is unacceptable under any circumstances.
One principle must remain clear:
Local authorities must never resort to excessive force, brutality or cruelty in carrying out their duties.
Whether a dog is a pet or a stray, licensed or unlicensed, every animal must be treated humanely.
I understand that there have been reports that Rocky's family had not obtained a licence for him.
If this is true, it should be addressed through the proper legal and administrative channels. However, two wrongs do not make a right.
The absence of a licence can never be used to justify the use of force or actions that result in unnecessary suffering and death.
This tragedy should serve as a wake-up call for local councils throughout Malaysia to review and improve dog-catching methods and  procedures.
Many of these procedures are outdated, archaic and fail to reflect modern standards of animal welfare and humane enforcement. Enforcement officers must be equipped not only with the tools but also with the skills to manage difficult situations with compassion, patience and professionalism.
Greater emphasis must be placed on de-escalation techniques, humane animal handling and conflict management.
Officers should be trained to assess situations, take the time to calm distressed animals and concerned owners, and avoid unnecessary confrontation whenever possible.
Had such principles been observed, Rocky's death may  have been prevented.
Local councils are entrusted with significant powers.
With those powers comes an equally important responsibility to act with compassion, mercy, restraint and respect for life.
Public confidence in local government can only be maintained when enforcement is carried out fairly, professionally and humanely.
Rocky's death must not be dismissed as an unfortunate incident.
It must be a catalyst for meaningful reform to ensure that such a tragedy never happens again.
NALINA NAIR
,
Councillor,
Petaling Jaya City Council
*The views expressed in this article are the author's own and do not necessarily reflect those of the New Straits Times

Title: 92 reports, 24 probe papers opened during Negri poll campaign
Article:
SEREMBAN: Police received 92 reports and opened 24 investigation papers during the campaign period for the Negri Sembilan election, which ended at midnight, says Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail.
He said most cases involved offences under the Election Offences Act, including acts of mischief such as damage to political parties' banners and flags.
"From nomination day on July 18 until today, we received 92 police reports and opened 24 investigation papers. Most involved acts of mischief, including damage to banners and flags belonging to contesting parties.
"Overall, the Negri Sembilan election has proceeded smoothly and orderly," he told reporters after visiting the polling centre at SMK King George V today.
Khalid said several other cases were being investigated under the Sedition Act and the Communications and Multimedia Act over campaign statements touching on sensitive and racial issues.
On allegations of cash handouts during the campaign period, he said police had received four reports so far.
"We are still investigating these reports by recording statements from those involved and gathering evidence to determine whether such incidents occurred," he said.
Also present were Bukit Aman Internal Security and Public Order Department director Datuk Seri Mohd Yusri Hassan Basri and Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Negri Sembilan polls: Polling day adds unique twist to Kuala Pilah couple's wedding
Article:
KUALA PILAH: A Negri Sembilan couple's wedding became even more memorable after their big day coincided with the state's polling day, prompting the groom to head to the ballot box before the marriage ceremony.
Dentist Zulhid Rosmawi, 32, said he and his family had fixed the wedding date about six months ago, long before the Election Commission announced Aug 1 as polling day.
"When the polling date was announced, I was surprised and a little anxious because it fell on our wedding day," he said at the wedding venue.
Despite the coincidence, Zulhid said preparations for the ceremony went ahead as planned.
"We decided to carry on as usual. I informed the venue management and our families that nothing would change, except we reminded guests to expect heavier traffic because of polling day," he said.
Determined to fulfil his civic duty before the ceremony, Zulhid arrived at the Kampung Jawa polling centre as early as 7.30am to cast his ballot.
"I wanted to avoid the crowds. Initially, I planned to vote after the wedding, but my wife felt it would be better to get it done early.
"I was among the first few voters there. Once the polling station opened, I went straight in," he said.
A Kuala Pilah native from Kampung Jawa, Zulhid said voting was a responsibility that should not be neglected, regardless of personal commitments.
"My advice to everyone is to go out and vote. Even though I'm busy with my wedding today, I still made sure to cast my ballot because it is our responsibility.
"We are choosing leaders who will represent and lead our area, so everyone should fulfil that responsibility," he said.
Zulhid's wife did not vote as she is from Kuala Lumpur.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: TH: 2017 accounts could have shown RM1.4bil loss under accounting rules
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) said its 2017 financial statement would have recorded a loss if it had fully adopted the Malaysian Financial Reporting Standards (MFRS).
In a statement today, TH said this was in response to the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on the agency, which raised concerns over the preparation of financial statements that did not fully comply with recognised accounting principles.
TH said the RCI's findings on the use of the Realisable Asset Value (RAV) method reinforced the need for financial statements to be prepared transparently, consistently and in accordance with established accounting standards.
"As a statutory body established under federal law, TH is subject to the Statutory Bodies (Accounts and Annual Reports) Act 1980 (Act 240), which requires financial statements to be prepared in accordance with recognised accounting principles.
"However, TH would have recorded a net loss of about RM1.4 billion, instead of the reported net profit of RM3.4 billion for the 2017 financial year, if MFRS had been fully applied at the time," it said.
The RCI report had previously found that the use of RAV created two different views of TH's financial position, and stated that the method was inconsistent with Section 22 of Act 535 relating to asset valuation as it was not reflected in TH's audited financial statements.
It also found that TH's profit distribution approach between 2014 and 2017 did not comply with Section 22 of Act 535, as distributions should have been based on actual profits rather than depositors' funds.
The practice affected TH's financial reserves and created expectations among depositors for consistently high dividend payouts, the report said.
TH's financial position between 2014 and 2017 showed its asset-liability deficit widening to RM4.093 billion from RM352 million.
Meanwhile, TH said it had implemented a policy since 2022 to declare profit distributions only based on audited financial statements, in line with the RCI's recommendations.
It said previous profit distributions were announced before audits were completed, which went against principles of good governance, transparency and financial sustainability.
"Profit distributions are now announced only after audited financial results are finalised, strengthening the integrity of the reporting process and increasing depositor confidence.
"TH continues to show positive progress following governance reforms, improved risk management and strengthened investment strategies and financial performance," it said.
TH said profit distributions rose to 3.25 per cent in 2024 before reaching 3.5 per cent last year, compared with 3.1 per cent for the 2023 financial year, marking the highest rate in eight years.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police to record Sanusi's statement in Kedah
Article:
SEREMBAN: Police will record the statement of Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor over remarks he allegedly made touching on racial issues during a political rally in Jempol recently.
Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said the case remained under investigation.
"We are trying to obtain a statement from the menteri besar himself.

He this matter requires further investigation and evidence from the relevant parties so that investigations are completed soon, before the case is submitted to the attorney-general," he said.

Title: Sisters turn polling day into patriotic parade of Jalur Gemilang [WATCH]
Article:
REMBAU: Two siblings turned heads at the polling centre in Sekolah Jenis Kebangsaan Cina (SJKC) Chung Hua, Rantau today after arriving dressed in Jalur Gemilang-themed outfits, adding a patriotic touch to the voting atmosphere.
The Rantau-born sisters decided to combine their civic duty with the spirit of the upcoming National Day celebrations.
Eldest sister Zamzarina Basiron, 45, said the idea came naturally as August marks the start of National Day celebrations.
"Since National Day is just around the corner, we wanted to bring a patriotic vibe through our outfits. I usually have clothes like this every year for the celebrations, so I invited my sisters to join me in creating a cheerful atmosphere while we cast our votes today," said Zamzarina, a teacher.
The sisters' coordinated outfits drew attention from fellow voters at the polling centre.
Younger sister Bahirah Basiron, 39, a food entrepreneur, said they spent about two days preparing their outfits and completing the look with Jalur Gemilang-themed accessories.
Meanwhile, youngest sister Nadzifah Basiron, 36, who works at Hospital Rembau, said she could not prepare a patriotic outfit in time due to work commitments but came along to support her sisters.
Voting for the Negri Sembilan election is proceeding smoothly today, with 859,760 registered voters, including 7,391 postal voters, eligible to cast their ballots.
The Election Commission is targeting a turnout of between 72 and 75 per cent, with preliminary results expected from 10pm and the full results before midnight.

Title: Malaysia's economy set to stay strong in 2H 2026, says Akmal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's economic performance is expected to remain strong in the second half of 2026 (2H 2026), supported by government measures to maintain stable oil supplies, says Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir.
He said the country recorded 5.6 per cent growth in the first half of 2026 (1H 2026), while Bank Negara Malaysia's projection for the year remains between 4.0 and 5.0 per cent.
"We have achieved 5.6 per cent economic growth in 1H 2026. We hope for the best in 2H 2026, but we must also be prepared for any possibility," he told reporters after attending the Association of Malaysian Economics Undergraduates (AMEU) Economics Summit 2026 today.
Akmal said Malaysia must remain cautious over unresolved geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, particularly developments involving the Strait of Hormuz, which continue to affect global oil supply.
According to the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM), the economy expanded 5.8 per cent in the second quarter of 2026 (2Q 2026), compared with 5.4 per cent in 1Q 2026, driven by stronger growth in the services and manufacturing sectors.
The economy grew 5.6 per cent in 1H 2026 compared with 4.5 per cent in the same period last year, supported by a recovery in the mining and quarrying sector, while construction activity continued to expand.
Meanwhile, Akmal said hosting a Formula One (F1) race was expected to boost economic growth, particularly through tourism.
He said major international events that attract foreign visitors would generate economic spillovers through tourist spending.
"Based on Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's emphasis, the benefits should not only go to certain segments but should also reach small traders," he said.
Last Sunday, F1 confirmed Malaysia as the host of the Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) from Oct 2 to 4, following agreements signed between F1, the International Automobile Federation (FIA), and the Malaysian and Bahraini governments.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Undang Luak Jelebu dismissed
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Dewan Keadilan dan Undang Negri Sembilan (DKU) has accepted the dismissal of Datuk Maarof Mat Rashad as the 16th  Undang Luak Jelebu over "adat offences".
The dismissal is effective from May 31, 2023.
In a statement, the council said the post of Undang Luak Jelebu was now deemed vacant, and that any action taken by Maarof after the date of his dismissal was considered invalid.
It also said Maarof had forfeited the Darjah Tertinggi Negeri Sembilan (DTNS), the state's highest honour, which he held by virtue of his office as the Undang Luak Jelebu.
"The state government is directed to act on the DKU's decisions," it said.
The dismissal of the Undang Luak Jelebu follows the recent dismissal of the former Undang Luak Sungai Ujong and the replacement of the former Undang Luak Rembau.
The matter was among several decisions made during a Dewan Keadilan dan Undang sitting on July 31, chaired by the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
The council also declared that an April 19 announcement on the removal of Tuanku Muhriz as the Yang di-Pertuan Besar, purportedly by the four Undang, was unconstitutional and therefore invalid.
It said Mubarak Thahak, Abdul Rahim Yasin and Maarof Mat Rashad, who were purportedly holding the posts of the Sungei Ujong, Rembau and Jelebu Undangs respectively, had either ceased to hold office or had never validly held the posts.
Yesterday's sitting was attended by the Undang Luak Sungai Ujong Muhammad Faris Johari, the Undang Luak Rembau Hassan Ab Hamid, and the Tunku Besar Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin Tuanku Muhriz, fulfilling the quorum requirement under Clause 20 of the Laws of the Constitution of Negri Sembilan.
Separately, the council also recognised the appointments of Faris and Hassan as the respective Undang for Sungai Ujong and Rembau. Both were installed on June 27.
It said both appointments had been made in accordance with the adat of their respective luak.
The council also took note that Datuk Seri Badarudin Abdul Khalid had been removed as the Datuk Shahbandar Sungei Ujong according to the adat of Luak Sungei Ujong, effective July 30.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Petronas fuel supply stable until September, says Azalina
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Fuel supplies, including petrol and diesel, at Petronas stations nationwide are expected to remain stable and sufficient until September, says Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Legal and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
She said the Petronas network, which is supplied through its listed subsidiary Petronas Dagangan Bhd, accounted for about 50 per cent of the country's domestic fuel needs.
The matter was reported at the weekly meeting of the National Economic Action Council (NEAC), she said in a written parliamentary reply published on the Dewan Negara website dated July 29.
Azalina said the Crisis Management Task Force (CMT) under NEAC continued to monitor fuel and energy supply amid the global energy crisis arising from the West Asia conflict.
She said the task force also ensured supply security in the coming months, while monitoring prices and preventing smuggling and illegal activities.
"Efforts are ongoing to secure crude oil supplies from exporters outside the Middle East, including West Africa and the Americas, subject to crude oil grade suitability and commercial terms," she said.
Azalina was responding to a question from Senator Tan Sri Low Kian Chuan on the long-term sustainability and diversification of Malaysia's petroleum resources, as well as Petronas' strategy to ensure energy security amid rising domestic fuel consumption.
On Malaysia's crude oil and natural gas reserves, she said Petronas estimated the country's crude oil reserves at 3.89 billion barrels of oil equivalent, while total natural gas reserves stood at 13.19 billion barrels of oil equivalent as of Jan 1, 2026.
Based on the estimated reserves and current production rates, Azalina said the lifespan of the reserves was expected to exceed 20 years.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar invites Mahatma Gandhi's grandson to visit Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has invited Rajmohan Gandhi, the grandson of Mahatma Gandhi, to visit Malaysia in the first quarter of next year to deliver a lecture on democracy, peace, harmony and values-based leadership.
In a social media post today, Anwar said he extended the invitation during a telephone conversation with the 91-year-old Rajmohan, an eminent historian and author.
Anwar said the lecture would provide an opportunity for academics, university students and community leaders to benefit from Rajmohan's perspectives on democracy, peaceful coexistence and principled leadership.
"I had the opportunity to have a telephone conversation with an old friend, Rajmohan Gandhi, who is also a historian and the grandson of Mahatma Gandhi.
"We reminisced about our meeting at the conference on democracy in Asia that he organised in Mumbai in 2012, while exchanging views on efforts to strengthen Malaysia-India historical and civilisational ties through academic and intellectual cooperation, as well as dialogue between civilisations," he said.
Anwar said they also exchanged views on strengthening the historical and civilisational ties between Malaysia and India through closer academic and intellectual collaboration, as well as dialogue between civilisations.
He expressed hope that their longstanding friendship would continue to flourish.
Rajmohan is an Indian historian, biographer and former member of the Rajya Sabha.
The Rajya Sabha, also known as Council of States, is the upper house of the Parliament of India, of which the Lok Sabha is the lower house. The Rajya Sabha represents India's federal units – the states and union territories.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Loke: Voters, not surveys, will decide Negri polls [WATCH]
Article:
SEREMBAN: The outcome of the Negri Sembilan election would ultimately be determined by voters, not pre-election opinion polls, says DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke.
Asked about an Ilham Centre survey that showed unfavourable findings for Pakatan Harapan, he said the people's decision remained the most important factor.
"Everyone has surveys, not just one. Different parties have their own surveys and methodologies. In the end, what matters is the people's decision, not the surveys.
"That is what we are waiting to see. We hope for the best possible outcome for PH tonight," he told reporters after casting his ballot for the Mambau seat at SJK(C) Kelpin, Taman Ujong, today.
On the voting process, Loke said polling had been smooth so far and expressed hope that turnout would surpass 75 per cent by 6pm.
He urged voters to come out and fulfil their responsibility, adding that strong participation was important to ensure the outcome reflected the majority's will.
"Based on the reports I received, some constituencies recorded higher turnout this morning, while others were lower.
"Whatever the outcome, it should reflect the will of the majority of voters," said Loke, who is also the PH candidate for the Chennah state seat.
Mambau is seeing a three-cornered contest, with PH's Lee Kai Yet facing Bersatu's N. Sarawanan and Parti Wawasan Negara's Erik Michael.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Eight illegal migrants caught after crossing from Thailand
Article:
PASIR PUTEH: Eight undocumented Indonesian migrants who entered Malaysia from Thailand were detained in an operation at a house in Kampung Gong Serapat here yesterday.
A man and woman, believed to be the house owners, were also arrested for allegedly harbouring the undocumented migrants.
General Operations Force Southeast Brigade commander Senior Assistant Commissioner Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the 10 suspects were arrested during the operation codenamed Op Taring Wawasan Kelantan.
"A GOF team from the Seventh Battalion raided the house at 7.20pm following a tip-off.
"Three Indonesian women were found hiding in the living room, while five Indonesian men were in a store behind the house.
"The eight failed to produce valid travel or identification documents when requested by police," he said.
He said the Indonesians comprised three women, aged between 38 and 55, and five men, aged between 20 and 56.
Initial investigations revealed they had entered Malaysia through an illegal jetty along the Kelantan River from Thailand on July 30 before being taken to the house.
The migrants claimed they had each paid an Indonesian agent RM4,000 to arrange their journey into Malaysia.
"They were heading to Kuala Lumpur to work as construction labourers and cleaners when arrested," he said.
Ahmad Radzi said police also seized 10 mobile phones worth RM22,000 during the operation.
The case is being investigated under Section 26J of the Anti-Trafficking in Persons and Anti-Smuggling of Migrants Act 2007 and Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63.
He said the suspects and the seized items had been handed over to the Pasir Puteh district police headquarters for further investigation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Civil servants begin hybrid work arrangement today [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Hybrid Workday (HBH) Policy for civil servants takes effect today, allowing employees to work three days in the office and two days from home or alternative locations.
The move marks a shift from the traditional five-day office arrangement to a hybrid model combining physical workplace attendance with remote working, as part of the public service reform agenda.
The Public Service Department (PSD) described the policy as a future-ready measure to ensure government services remain resilient amid global changes and evolving work practices, while maintaining service quality.
Under the HBH implementation guidelines, states observing Sunday as the weekly holiday will have Monday and Friday designated as mandatory office attendance days.
For Kedah, Kelantan and Terengganu, Sundays and Thursdays will be compulsory office attendance days.
The remaining office attendance day will be determined by the respective heads of department, while the other two days may be allocated for work from home (WFH), subject to job suitability and stipulated conditions.
The hybrid arrangement is already practised in several developed countries, including Singapore, Australia, Finland and Sweden.
Eligible officers no longer need to apply for approval, as HBH is now part of the permanent work arrangement, subject to conditions set by their respective heads of department.
Heads of department have the authority to determine eligibility, require officers to report to the office on WFH days when necessary, or withdraw the arrangement if conditions are not met.
However, the policy does not apply to essential services requiring full physical presence, including counter services, security forces, defence, enforcement, education, healthcare and the courts.
To ensure productivity, officers' attendance and work output will be monitored through the SPOT-Me system. Officers are also required to comply with the Official Secrets Act 1972, remain contactable and report to the office when directed.
PSD previously said the HBH policy would be based on trust, integrity and accountability, supported by digital technology to ensure uninterrupted and quality government service delivery.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bersatu can win several seats today, says Tun Faisal
Article:
SEREMBAN: A Bersatu leader has voiced confidence that the party can win several seats in today's Negri Sembilan election.
Its information chief, Datuk Tun Faisal Ismail Aziz, said this confidence stemmed from positive voter response towards the party's candidates.
"Hopefully, this positive reception can be translated into votes today," he said when met by reporters at Institut Perguruan Raja Melewar in Sikamat here this morning.
Tun Faisal, who is contesting the Sikamat seat, said he would leverage his experience in government to serve the constituency should he win.
The Sikamat seat sees a three-cornered fight between Tun Faisal, Pakatan Harapan's Nor Azman Mohamad and Perikatan Nasional's Datuk Razali Abu Samah.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Masidi: 40pct revenue issue likely to come up at Monday's Sabah-Putrajaya meet
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Sabah will meet with the federal government on Monday to discuss matters related to the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63), says Deputy Chief Minister Datuk Seri Masidi Manjun.
"During that meeting, I am confident that the 40 per cent revenue entitlement will be mentioned.
"For now, I would like to inform you that the state and federal governments are actively engaged in discussions to ensure that the allocation announced by the prime minister (Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim) can be paid this year," he told a press conference here.
Earlier, Masidi represented Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor at the launch of the state-level National Day and Sabah Day celebrations.
Last week, the state assembly was told that Sabah had received
RM600 million
of the RM1.5 billion special grant promised by Anwar.
In April, the Court of Appeal allowed the federal government's application to stay a
High Court order
requiring a review of Sabah's 40 per cent revenue entitlement.
The Kota Kinabalu High Court had on Oct 17, 2025, ruled that the federal government acted unlawfully by failing to honour Sabah's right to 40 per cent of federal revenue from 1974 to 2021.
On Hajiji's message that love for Sabah is inseparable from patriotism towards the nation, Masidi said the two sentiments are indivisible because Sabah is part of Malaysia.
When asked whether Sabahans' strong state identity could stem from unequal development, Masidi said it was more important to ensure Sabah was at the forefront of, and part and parcel of, the country's overall development agenda.
"I'm not in the blame game or against it. I think eventually Malaysians, including Sabahans, should ask themselves what they have done to contribute to the overall development of the country."
Responding to comments by several assemblymen that Sabah should not emulate Sarawak, particularly in terms of policies and development, Masidi said an "apple-to-apple" comparison could not be made between the two states.
He added that every state has a different development agenda.
"What suits one state may not suit another. The sort of development we have in Sabah is tailor-made for Sabah.
"When people offer criticism or opinions, they should also come up with solutions. I believe most Sabahans are patriotic."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Last year I lost my son, now his wife and child are gone too'
Article:
KOTA BARU: A family still mourning the loss of its patriarch last year has been hit by another tragedy after a mother and her youngest son were killed in a road accident in Gua Musang on Friday.
Maria Yusoff, 42, and her 11-year-old son Muhammad Ziekry Iman Abli were among three people killed when the Perodua Myvi they were travelling in collided with a diesel tanker at Km25 of the Gua Musang-Kuala Krai road at 7am.
Maria's mother-in-law, Rokiah Jusoh, 76, said the tragedy came less than a year after her son, Abli Abdullah, died suddenly from a heart attack on July 27 last year.
"My grandchildren had only just marked one year since losing their father. Now they have lost their mother and youngest sibling too. They became orphans in the blink of an eye," she said when met at her home in Kampung Kubang Tin, Melor, today.
Rokiah said the family initially withheld news of Maria's death, fearing the shock could affect her health.
"They asked me to recite the syahadah and seek forgiveness before telling me what happened. I accepted it with a heavy heart. After losing my son last year, God has now taken his wife and child too," she said.
She said Maria, who had four children, had travelled to Cameron Highlands with her eldest daughter Nur Balqis Abli, 21, and youngest son Muhammad Ziekry. Her second and third children did not join the trip as they had fever.
Rokiah recalled that before leaving, Maria had mentioned her intention to settle debts owed to relatives and friends.
"I told her to pay only if she could afford it, but she said she had already cleared RM500 in debts," she said.
Rokiah said she would now care for her two surviving grandchildren following the deaths of both their parents.
Maria and Muhammad Ziekry were laid to rest at the Melor Lama Muslim Cemetery at 8.30am today.
The third victim, car driver Muhamad Hakimi Syazwan Ibrahim, was buried at the Kampung Tegayung Barat Muslim Cemetery at about the same time.
Earlier, the remains of all three victims arrived at their respective villages at 2.51am after post-mortem examinations at Gua Musang Hospital.
Hakimi's father, Ibrahim Daud, 69, said he only learnt of his son's plan to visit Cameron Highlands after being informed by his wife shortly before receiving news of the fatal crash.
"He had hoped to continue his studies after completing his course at the Terengganu Industrial Training Institute, but that dream was never realised. I am still in shock, but I accept God's will," he said.
Nur Balqis is currently warded at Hospital Kuala Krai and has been placed in an induced coma after suffering severe head injuries.
Yesterday, it was reported that three people were killed after a car collided with a diesel tanker in the
7am crash
on Friday.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Govt success measured by people's gains, says Hajiji
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: The true measure of a government's success lies in how much its people benefit from development, says Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor.
He said the state government would continue strengthening initiatives that directly impact lives, including in education, welfare, housing, healthcare, rural development, women and youth empowerment, and basic amenities.
"Ultimately, the true measure of a government's success is not what it has built, but the extent to which the people benefit from that development," he said in a speech delivered by Deputy Chief Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Masidi Manjun.
"I am confident that with the spirit of togetherness, integrity in governance, close cooperation between the state and federal governments, and the unwavering support of the people, we can take Sabah further forward as a more advanced and prosperous state."
The speech was delivered in conjunction with the launch of the state-level National Day and Sabah Day celebrations.
Hajiji added that in the digital era, the public had greater opportunities to express their views and stay informed about the state's development.
"The state government values every opinion and constructive criticism as a reflection of the people's concern for Sabah's future.
"However, all views should be expressed responsibly, based on verified facts and with the intention of building rather than dividing society.
"Let us make wise use of technology to disseminate accurate information, foster mutual understanding and strengthen unity," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: EC chairman monitors Negri polls as voting gets underway
Article:
SEREMBAN: Election Commission (EC) chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun today visited three polling centres in Seremban to monitor the voting process and ensure the 16th Negri Sembilan election runs smoothly and orderly.
He began his inspection at Sekolah Kebangsaan Taman Paroi Jaya, serving the Sikamat state constituency, at 9.30am.
Ramlan then visited Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan Agama Sheikh Haji Mohd Said, also in Sikamat, before concluding his tour at Sekolah Menengah Agama (SMA) Dato' Klana Petra Maamor, which serves the Ampangan constituency.
During the visits, he received briefings from election officials on the voting process and inspected facilities provided for voters and election personnel.
He is also scheduled to observe the pilot implementation of the Voter Attendance Optical Character Recognition (OCR-VA) system at polling streams 1 to 7 at the SMA Dato' Klana Petra Maamor polling centre.
The OCR-VA system was developed to record and verify voter attendance by automatically scanning information from identity cards, with the aim of improving election management efficiency.
As of 10am, voter turnout stood at 18.22 per cent.
The EC is targeting an overall turnout of between 72 and 75 per cent. Preliminary results are expected as early as 10pm, with the full results expected before midnight.
A total of 859,760 registered voters, including 7,391 postal voters, are eligible to cast their ballots today to elect representatives for the state's 36 legislative assembly seats, with 103 candidates contesting.
Early voting on July 28 recorded a turnout of 91.06 per cent, or 14,995 voters, surpassing the EC's 90 per cent target.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump's legal crusade against news media falters
Article:
NEW YORK: Donald Trump's early legal wins against broadcasters ABC and CBS have given way to defeats and retreats as courts and newsrooms act to protect press freedom.
"News organisations recognise that the only positive outcome to this is prevailing against the president and standing up for the reporters and their newsrooms," said Ken Paulson, director of the Free Speech Centre at Middle Tennessee State University.
At the end of July, the Justice Department withdrew subpoenas issued to New York Times journalists who had written articles about the security of Trump's presidential aircraft.
It was forced to act after a federal judge slammed the administration's sloppy legal work and found it violated protections granted to journalists and their sources.
The president has also filed defamation suits targeting The New York Times over articles and a book about the origins of his fortune, and The Wall Street Journal over an article about a salacious letter he sent to Jeffrey Epstein. Both are floundering.
"If you're willing to stand up to Trump, you're going to do fairly well in court, given the lack of merit behind the cases that he has filed," observed Dan Kennedy, a journalism professor at Northeastern University in Massachusetts.
The cases involving ABC and CBS ended in December 2024 and July 2025 with the broadcasters agreeing to pay US$15 million and US$16 million, respectively.
Trump sued ABC for defamation over statements about a civil judgment against him in a sexual assault case. He took CBS to court for allegedly misleading viewers by airing different clips of the same answer from an interview with 2024 Democratic presidential candidate Kamala Harris.
But most legal experts agree that the courts could have thrown out Trump's claims.
Both reached the settlements "for business reasons," said Kennedy.
CBS's parent company, Paramount Global, for instance, was seeking regulatory approval for its merger with Skydance.
SUBPOENAS, LAWSUITS PART OF MEDIA STRATEGY
After ABC kept talk show host Jimmy Kimmel, a nightly critic of Trump, on the air, and elected not to broadcast a live Trump speech about alleged electoral fraud, the network now faces threats to some of its local station licences from federal authorities.
In another case, the BBC, which the US president is suing for US$10 billion over an allegedly misleading edit of one of his speeches, has adopted a strategy that experts expect to become more widespread.
The British broadcaster is demanding that Trump's legal team produce financial documents to quantify the damages suffered.
"That is the biggest deterrent of all for a man who has constantly resisted efforts to look inside his empire and financial circumstances," said Paulson.
Trump's real objective, however, is not to win the lawsuits, experts say.
"You go right back to the beginning of his political career, 11-12 years ago, and it's been a central part of his strategy to discredit the news media," said Kennedy.
"He does that by insulting them, calling them fake news, calling them enemies of the people, and he does it by filing lawsuits."
Paulson said that "Trump and his lawyers have no realistic expectation that they will prevail in a court of law somewhere down the road."
"But that can take years and millions of dollars, and Trump knows from his business experience that if he can apply enough pressure, someone will cough up a cheque."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: ‘Shared responsibility’: Hannah Yeoh urges public to help maintain cleanliness during Putrajaya National Day celebration
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 1 — Members of the public attending the 2026 National Day celebration at Dataran Putrajaya on Aug 31 have been urged to act responsibly by disposing of their rubbish at designated areas to ensure the venue remains clean.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said she does not want a repeat of the recent incident at Dataran Merdeka, Kuala Lumpur, where large amounts of rubbish were left behind following a public gathering.
“Maintaining cleanliness is a shared responsibility. It is not solely the responsibility of Putrajaya Corporation (PPj) to collect rubbish after an event.
“Imagine coming to celebrate National Day, only to leave behind an area covered with rubbish. I do not think that creates a good impression, and I urge everyone present to dispose of their waste in the bins provided,” she told reporters after officiating the Madani Kita (PMK) programme with the Putrajaya Federal Territory community today.
The event was also attended by PPj president Datuk Mohd Sakeri Abdul Kadir.
During the programme, Hannah presented mock cheques representing a special contribution of RM5,000 from Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to selected Kawasan Rukun Tetangga (KRT) or Neighbourhood Watch areas.
Hannah said her office is currently focusing on efforts to raise public awareness and believes the public has learned from the recent rubbish accumulation incident at Dataran Merdeka.
She added that PPj would increase the number of rubbish bins at strategic locations and enhance waste collection frequency to ensure the celebration area remains clean and comfortable.
“I will also ensure that PPj issues reminders and announcements to everyone present to dispose of their rubbish properly. This is a shared responsibility and not just the duty of local authorities to clean up after an event,” she said.
On July 20, Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) conducted cleanup operations at Dataran Merdeka after the area was left littered following a large gathering to watch the live broadcast of the 2026 FIFA World Cup final.
DBKL said waste collection would continue, but stressed that maintaining the cleanliness of the capital should not depend solely on the efforts of cleaning workers after the public has left.
The 2026 National Day celebration would be held at Dataran Putrajaya on Aug 31 on a moderate yet vibrant scale.
“Malaysia Madani: Kesejahteraan Dinikmati” has been selected as the theme for the 2026 National Day and Malaysia Day (HKHM2026) celebrations, while the Malaysia Madani logo will continue to be used as the official logo for the celebrations until next year. — Bernama

Title: Bukit Aman awaits Indonesian details after Malaysian pilot arrested with drugs at Jakarta airport
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 1 — Bukit Aman will cooperate with Indonesian authorities following the arrest of a Malaysian pilot accused of attempting to smuggle drugs into the country.
Narcotic Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said police are awaiting further details from their counterparts before determining the next course of action, the
New Straits Times
(NST) reported.
He explained that officers were considering whether to send a team of investigators to Indonesia to interview the suspect and establish the full circumstances of the case. The inquiry would examine where the drugs were obtained and whether the pilot was acting alone or in collaboration with a trafficking syndicate.
Hussein told NST that investigators also wanted to determine how many times the suspect might have carried out similar operations and whether he was part of a wider network.
Investigators are also examining how the suspect allegedly managed to pass through airport security in Malaysia before departing for Indonesia.
AFP reported that the 39-year-old pilot, identified only as MSO, was arrested at Jakarta’s Soekarno Hatta International Airport with more than 70,000 ecstasy pills in his luggage and a small amount of methamphetamine in his hand baggage.
Customs officials said his urine test was positive for multiple drugs, and investigators revealed he admitted this was his third smuggling attempt, including two to Indonesia and one in Malaysia.

Title: Chief Justice heads Pahang state honours list
Article:
KUANTAN, Aug 1 — Chief Justice Tun Wan Ahmad Farid Wan Salleh heads the list of 52 recipients of Pahang state honours, awards and medals, in an investiture ceremony held in conjunction with the 67th birthday celebration of Sultan Pahang Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri’ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah.
Al-Sultan Abdullah presented the awards at Balai Mahkota, Istana Abdulaziz here today.
Also present were the Tengku Ampuan of Pahang, Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah and the Tengku Mahkota of Pahang, Tengku Hassanal Ibrahim Alam Shah.
Pahang Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail and state government leaders were also in attendance.
Wan Ahmad Farid was conferred the Sri Setia Al-Sultan Abdullah Ahmad Shah Pahang (SAAS) award, which carries the title of Datuk Seri Setia.
The Sri Sultan Ahmad Shah Pahang (SSAP) award, which carries the title of Datuk Seri, was conferred on 16 individuals, including Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi and Dewan Rakyat deputy speaker Datuk Dr Ramli Mohd Nor, who is also the Cameron Highlands MP.
Also receiving the SSAP award were Deputy Minister of Economy and Paya Besar MP Datuk Mohd Shahar Abdullah and Pahang Local Government, Housing, Environment and Green Technology Committee chairman Datuk Mohammad Fakhruddin Mohd Ariff.
Other recipients included Army Chief General Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman, Royal Malaysian Customs Department director-general Datuk Amran Ahmad, Local Government Department director-general Datuk Mohd Fadzli Mohd Kenali and International Islamic University Malaysia rector Professor Emeritus Datuk Dr Osman Bakar.
Joining the list of SSAP recipients were Universiti Tun Abdul Razak (UniRazak) chancellor Datuk Mohamed Nizam Abdul Razak, Armed Forces Joint Forces commander Lieutenant-General Datuk Tengku Muhammad Fauzi Tengku Ibrahim and Deputy Air Force Chief Lieutenant General Datuk Nur Hafis Abdul Karim.
Also receiving the honour were Air Education and Training commander Lieutenant General Datuk Muhammad Tarminzi Mustapha and singer Datuk Shaheila Abdul Majid, better known as Sheila Majid.
The Sultan of Pahang also conferred the Sri Indera Mahkota Pahang (SIMP) award, which carries the title of Datuk Indera, on two recipients, namely Koperasi Serbausha Makmur Berhad (Kosma) chairman Datuk Zamri Mohamed and Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation (MATRADE) chief executive officer Datuk Abu Bakar Yusof.
Eight individuals were conferred the Darjah Sultan Ahmad Shah Pahang (DSAP) award, which carries the title of Datuk, including Pahang Syariah Chief Judge Datuk Abdul Walid Abu Hassan, Naval Area 1 commander Rear Admiral Azman Rabani and Faiza Sdn Bhd managing director Faiza Bawumi Sayed Ahmad.
Pahang Communications and Multimedia, Youth, Sports and Non-Governmental Organisation Committee chairman Fadzli Mohamad Kamal was among 18 recipients conferred the Darjah Indera Mahkota Pahang (DIMP) award, which carries the title of Datuk.
Other recipients of the DIMP award included Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department Deputy Director-General (Operations) Nordin Pauzi, Pahang Education director Ahmad Zamri Md Isa and Tenaga Nasional Berhad Pahang general manager Affendi Abdul Rahman.
Also receiving the DIMP award were MFDM Holdings Sdn Bhd director Mohd Qabil Ambak Mahamad Fathil, who is also an equestrian athlete, and national silat exponent Mohd Al-Jufferi Jamari.
During the ceremony, the Sultan of Pahang also conferred the Setia Ahmad Shah Pahang (SAP) award on two recipients, the Setia Mahkota Pahang (SMP) award on one recipient, and the Ahli Ahmad Shah Pahang (AAP) and Ahli Mahkota Pahang (AMP) awards on two recipients each. — Bernama

Title: Police tighten security at Negeri Sembilan palace, state offices ahead of poll results
Article:
SEREMBAN, Aug 1 — Police will tighten security at key locations, including the Istana of the Yang di Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan and state government offices, to prevent any untoward incidents when the Negeri Sembilan state election results are announced later tonight.
Inspector General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said there was a possibility that certain quarters might attempt to stir tensions if dissatisfied with the outcome,
Sinar Harian
reported.
“After the election, there may be parties who turn hostile towards one another if there are changes in leadership, or if winners and losers are unhappy with the results. That is what concerns us,” he was quoted as saying.
Mohd Khalid was speaking to reporters after visiting the polling centre at Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan King George V here today.
He reminded party supporters to remain disciplined and obey instructions from the authorities to keep public safety in check.
The IGP also confirmed that the voting process so far had proceeded smoothly.

Title: Negeri Sembilan confirms two Undang appointments, declares three other claimants invalid
Article:
SEREMBAN, Aug 1 — The Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU) has formally recognised two newly installed Undang and declared three individuals who claimed the titles of Undang Sungei Ujong, Rembau and Jelebu as never having held those positions lawfully.
The decisions were issued following a DKU sitting on July 31, 2026, chaired by Yang di‑Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, convened with full quorum as required under the Negeri Sembilan Constitution 1959.
Muhammad Faris Johari was formerly recognised as the Undang Luak Sungei Ujong, while Raja Hassan Ab Hamid’s appointment as Undang Luak Rembau was also affirmed under adat.
The DKU also noted that the position of the position of Undang for Sungei Ujong is now vacant after the previous holder, Datuk Seri Badarudin Abdul Khalid, was removed according to adat effective 30 July 2026. The process to appoint a successor has not yet been completed.
In Jelebu, the council accepted the unanimous decision of Waris Berundang from the three perut — Kemin Teriang, Kemin Beringin and Kemin Bemban — to dismiss Datuk Maarof Mat Rashad as the 16th Undang Luak Jelebu, effective 31 May 2023, citing breaches of adat. All actions taken by him after that date are deemed invalid, and his use of the Darjah Tertinggi Negeri Sembilan (DTNS) is considered void. The state government has been instructed to act accordingly.
The DKU further ruled that a public announcement dated 19 April 2026 was unconstitutional and in violation of Article X of the Negeri Sembilan Constitution, rendering it null and without effect.
In its concluding declaration, the council stated that Mubarak Thahak, Abdul Rahim Yasin, and Maarof Mat Rashad had either ceased to hold or never lawfully held the positions of Undang for Sungei Ujong, Rembau and Jelebu respectively. As such, they possess no legal authority to exercise any powers under Article X of the state constitution.
The statement was issued by the DKU Secretary on August 1, 2026.

Title: Negeri Sembilan election sees 37pc voter turnout by noon
Article:
SEREMBAN, Aug 1 — A total of 37.29 per cent, or 320,627 of the 859,760 registered voters, had cast their ballots in the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election as of noon today.
The Election Commission (EC), in a Facebook post, said the Juasseh constituency recorded the highest voter turnout so far at 43.5 per cent, followed by Chennah (43.4 per cent) and Senaling (42.8 per cent).
The Lukut constituency recorded the lowest turnout at about 32.1 per cent.
For comparison, voter turnout at the same time during the 15th Negeri Sembilan state election stood at 35.44 per cent, or 297,024 of the 838,200 registered voters.
For the latest updates on the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election, visit https://prn.bernama.com/n9. — Bernama

Title: Johor Bahru police seek e‑hailing driver to identify passenger accused of insulting Islam
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 1 — Police are tracking down an e-hailing driver to assist in the investigation and identify a suspect linked to a viral video containing remarks allegedly insulting Islam in Johor Bahru.
Johor Bahru Selatan police chief ACP Azrul Hisham Mohd Shaffei said the district police headquarters received a report from a police officer at 3.25pm on July 31 after the officer came across the video on social media at about 2.30pm the same day.
He said the report was lodged as the content had sparked public concern for touching on religious sensitivities and allegedly insulting Islam.
“Preliminary investigations found that the incident took place at about 5.55pm on July 30 in Johor Bahru, based on dashcam footage capturing a conversation between a man believed to be an e-hailing driver and another man suspected to be his passenger,” he said in a statement today.
According to Azrul Hisham, the passenger is alleged to have made remarks insulting Islam and the Quran during the conversation.
He said police are now working to locate the e-hailing driver to assist in the investigation and help identify the suspect.
The case is being investigated under Section 4(1) of the Sedition Act 1948, Section 298 of the Penal Code, and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.
Police have urged the public not to speculate or disseminate unverified information that could jeopardise public order or interfere with the investigation.
Anyone with information related to the incident is urged to contact the Johor Bahru Selatan Police Headquarters hotline at 07-2182323 or report the matter at the nearest police station. — Bernama

Title: Sisters steal the spotlight in Rantau, casting votes in Jalur Gemilang style ahead of Merdeka
Article:
REMBAU, Aug 1 — In a vibrant display of national pride, two siblings turned heads at the polling centre in Sekolah Jenis Kebangsaan Cina (SJKC) Chung Hua, Rantau today when they showed up dressed head-to-toe in Jalur Gemilang-themed attire, adding a festive splash to the occasion.
Born and raised in Rantau, the duo decided to infuse their civic duty with the patriotic spirit of the upcoming National Day celebrations. Eldest sister Zamzarina Basiron, 45, explained that the idea came naturally.
“Since we’ve just entered August and National Day is just around the corner, we wanted to inject a patriotic vibe into our clothing. I actually have outfits like this every year for the celebrations, so I invited my sisters to join me in brightening up the atmosphere while we cast our votes today,” said Zamzarina, who is a teacher.
The sisters’ coordinated effort certainly paid off, drawing admiring glances from fellow voters at the polling station.
Younger sister Bahirah Basiron, 39, a food entrepreneur, said they spent about two days preparing the outfits and completing the look with various Jalur Gemilang-themed accessories.
Meanwhile, Nadzifah Basiron, 36, the youngest of the three siblings and a Hospital Rembau staff member, admitted she could not get a patriotic outfit in time due to work commitments, but still showed up to support her sisters.
Voting for the Negeri Sembilan state election is proceeding smoothly today, with 859,760 registered voters, including 7,391 postal voters, expected to cast their ballots.
The Election Commission targets a 72 to 75 per cent turnout, with preliminary results due by 10 pm and full results before midnight.
